cases.detail: Three equal revenue lines sharing a ten dollar payment create a leftover cent after flooring exact shares. The cent must go to the lexically first line id so nightly invoice exports remain stable.
cases.title: fractional cents

cases.detail: Customer credits arrive as positive source amounts because the upstream accounting feed stores the sign in the payment kind. Allocation rows carry the signed effect, so credits are negative allocations.
cases.title: credit memo sign

cases.detail: Discount and zero-dollar rows stay in invoice reports, but they never earn a share of customer cash and never dilute the denominator used for positive charge lines.
cases.title: adjustment lines

cases.detail: A card payment, an account credit, and a manual write-off may all touch the same invoice. Allocation rows should preserve payment order and payment ids so reconciliations can be traced.
cases.title: multiple tenders

cases.detail: Binary floats have caused one-cent drift in production exports. All money arithmetic should use Decimal or integer cents until the final Decimal dollar values are built.
cases.title: decimal safety
